analysis:
The supplied units are base-side excerpts of historical CHANGELOG.md release notes (base lines 1444-1910, v0.9.x entries). The PR's actual changed lines are at the top of the file (head 11-100, a new v0.10.1 candidate section). Only the truncated patch excerpt shows that new text, so the changed content is mostly outside the supplied evidence. I found no executable code, configuration, or enforced control in these units. I found no concrete security regression and no invalidated threat-model assumption.

From the visible patch excerpt, the new v0.10.1 section is documentation only, covering rollout notes: a coordinator dependency (darkbloom-platform#411) for logprobs refusal, an mlx-swift-lm pin bump, and page-cache accounting that now applies to every model. These are claims about behavior in other files that I could not see. I cannot verify them here. The excerpt cuts off in the page-cache accounting item, which says load admission, KV budgets, cold-load capacity and status/doctor can count more memory as available. If that change is real, it touches TB-007 memory safeguards and availability (T-029/T-016 class). That belongs to the source changes, not to this changelog.

The base-side historical text describes App Attest (TB-011, T-053, T-054, T-057), the encrypted SSD prefix cache (T-041, SEC-035), and diagnostics outside the signed transcript. I checked it for consistency with the supplied definitions and found nothing contradictory. It states diagnostics do not affect authorization, which matches T-052/T-058. It also states the 30-minute sliding TTL, which matches T-041.
